deviations.what: Round 3 stores a sanitized repository taskbook instead of the raw originating task transcript.
deviations.why: The raw transcript contains private local paths that the repository contamination policy forbids.
deviations.impact: A clone contains the complete audit contract with aliases, while line-by-line comparison to the original wording still requires the originating task transcript.

deviations.what: The real corpus used an abstract-only first version, a PDF-derived Markdown middle version, and a text third version.
deviations.why: The author explicitly prioritized content and selected these authorities after Stage 1 preparation.
deviations.impact: This supersedes the initial three-TeX extraction assumption without modifying any source TeX.

deviations.what: Stage 3 used two evaluation tracks instead of a single convergence headline.
deviations.why: Raw cross-version pairs changed facts and claim scope, so they were unsuitable as style-only efficacy ground truth.
deviations.impact: Do-no-harm is measured by Stage 3C; rule-direction change is measured by Stage 3D.

deviations.what: Stage 3D targets are author-approved, AI-assisted, style-only targets rather than raw third-version ground truth.
deviations.why: This preserves immutable facts and isolates P3-P5 style behavior.
deviations.impact: The 83.3333% metric applies only to rule-direction distance.

deviations.what: The first Stage 3D evaluator attempt stopped on a profile-hash prefix representation mismatch; only that harness comparison was repaired before the authorized rerun.
deviations.why: The trace used a qualified sha256 value while the manifest stored a bare digest.
deviations.impact: Frozen outputs were not regenerated; the subsequent single evaluation completed successfully.

deviations.what: No structural convergence percentage is reported.
deviations.why: Structural metric coverage is insufficient and one case has a zero denominator.
deviations.impact: The report avoids turning a sparse diagnostic into a capability claim.

deviations.what: The earlier one-off synthetic fixture that produced a 61.6% value was not preserved byte-for-byte.
deviations.why: It had already been deleted before Stage 4 and was absent from reachable repository history.
deviations.impact: Stage 4 rebuilt a current-contract regression suite and does not reuse that value as evidence.

deviations.what: evals and handoff are repository-only and excluded from installed skill payloads.
deviations.why: They are audit assets, not runtime dependencies, and may contain repository test metadata.
deviations.impact: Installed integrity does not require these directories; repository checks do.

deviations.what: head_commit intentionally identifies the audited implementation commit rather than the metadata-only commit containing this handoff.
deviations.why: Embedding the containing commit's own hash would be self-referential and cannot be made stable.
deviations.impact: Auditors resolve the containing commit from checkout HEAD and verify that its diff from head_commit is limited to handoff/.

deviations.what: The Stage 4 stop report used a Windows-backslash tree digest; Round 3 handoff replaces it with a POSIX-path digest.
deviations.why: The file set and file hashes were identical, but the relative path separator inside the hash manifest was platform-dependent.
deviations.impact: The canonical hash is now reproducible across operating systems; the earlier digest remains a Windows-path representation only.
